hint.description: Required audience-neutral, non-normative guidance. It must not add requirements absent from input_schema.

com_godaddy_shopping_input_schema_input_.description: A submitted line-item value. Object-shaped purchase input MUST include the root type discriminator required by its selected variant schema. The Checkout application validates the value against that schema during create and update.

context.description: Provisional buyer signals for relevance and localization—not authoritative data. Businesses SHOULD use these values when verified inputs (e.g., shipping address) are absent, and MAY ignore or down-rank them if inconsistent with higher-confidence signals (authenticated account, risk detection) or regulatory constraints (export controls). Eligibility and policy enforcement MUST occur at checkout time using binding transaction data. Context SHOULD be non-identifying and can be disclosed progressively—coarse signals early, finer resolution as the session progresses. Higher-resolution data (shipping address, billing address) supersedes context.

address_country.description: The country. Recommended to be in 2-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format, for example "US". For backward compatibility, a 3-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code such as "SGP" or a full country name such as "Singapore" can also be used. Optional hint for market context (currency, availability, pricing)—higher-resolution data (e.g., shipping address) supersedes this value.

address_region.description: The region in which the locality is, and which is in the country. For example, California or another appropriate first-level Administrative division. Optional hint for progressive localization—higher-resolution data (e.g., shipping address) supersedes this value.

currency.description: Preferred currency (ISO 4217, e.g., 'EUR', 'USD'). Businesses determine presentment currency from context and authoritative signals; this hint MAY inform selection in multi-currency markets. Also serves as the denomination for price filter values — platforms SHOULD include this field when sending price filters. Response prices include explicit currency confirming the resolution.

eligibility.description: Buyer claims about eligible benefits such as loyalty membership, payment instrument perks, and similar. Recognized claims MAY inform the Business response (e.g., member-only product availability, adjusted pricing in catalog, provisional discounts at cart or checkout). Businesses MUST ignore unrecognized values without error. Values MUST use reverse-domain naming (e.g., 'com.example.loyalty_gold', 'org.school.student') and MUST be non-identifying.

intent.description: Background context describing buyer's intent (e.g., 'looking for a gift under $50', 'need something durable for outdoor use'). Informs relevance, recommendations, and personalization.

language.description: Preferred language for content. Use IETF BCP 47 language tags (e.g., 'en', 'fr-CA', 'zh-Hans'). For REST, equivalent to Accept-Language header—platforms SHOULD fall back to Accept-Language when this field is absent; when provided, overrides Accept-Language. Businesses MAY return content in a different language if unavailable.

postal_code.description: The postal code. For example, 94043. Optional hint for regional refinement—higher-resolution data (e.g., shipping address) supersedes this value.

context.title: Context

description.description: Description content in one or more formats. At least one format must be provided.

html.description: HTML-formatted content. Security: Platforms MUST sanitize before rendering—strip scripts, event handlers, and untrusted elements. Treat all rich text as untrusted input.

description.title: Description

info.description:
GoDaddy Shopping REST API contract for Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).
This document is GoDaddy API product version 1.0.0; the UCP protocol version
is pinned separately in `ucp.version` on every response and in the
`requires.protocol` constraint of every extension schema.

The UCP 2026-04-08 schema dependency closure is vendored under
`schemas/ucp/`; each copied document retains its upstream canonical `$id`.
Compatible GoDaddy adaptations are made only in those vendored UCP documents
or in negotiated GoDaddy extension schemas; this OpenAPI document directly
references the vendored UCP contracts and retains only transport wiring and
endpoint-exclusive response composition.

GoDaddy-owned schemas use repository-relative `$ref` values. Their published identifiers use the
`https://godaddy.com/ucp/...` namespace (apex authority required by UCP
reverse-domain binding). GoDaddy extensions are available only after
capability negotiation; the GoDaddy UCP business profile (including the
`/.well-known/ucp` discovery endpoint) is maintained in
`gdcorp-platform/ucp-provider-specification`.

**Registered platform-standard deviations (forced by UCP protocol):**

1. **Error model** — UCP models business-logic failure as `200` with a `oneOf`
   between the success shape and `error_response` (`{messages: [...]}`). This
   deviates from GoDaddy's `error.json` must-have and conventional `4xx` codes
   for business errors. Deviation is forced by the protocol for every negotiated
   operation; the platform `error.json` pattern cannot apply to a UCP response
   envelope. Registered deviation.

2. **Transport errors** — `401`, `404`, and `429` responses also use UCP's
   `error_response` shape for consistency, which is a second deviation from the
   platform standard. This is a defensible consistency choice within the same
   protocol adapter. Registered deviation.

3. **`Request-Id` required** — Platform standard sets `required: false` on
   correlation headers (gateway enforces). UCP mandates `Request-Id` as
   `required: true` on all service operations. Deviation is forced by the
   protocol. Registered deviation.

4. **Pagination** — UCP-native `search_catalog` specifies cursor-based pagination
   (`cursor` / `limit` / `has_next_page`) in place of GoDaddy platform-standard
   offset pagination (`pageSize` / `page`) and HATEOAS `links` response fields.
   Deviation is forced by the UCP protocol shape for `search_catalog`. Registered deviation.

5. **`action_required` container** — UCP `2026-04-08` has no native product
   `actions` map. GoDaddy ships a bespoke `com.godaddy.shopping.catalog_action`
   extension carrying `product.action_required` as a temporary vendor bridge.
   Migration to the upstream native `actions` map will be evaluated at the next
   approved UCP-baseline upgrade; see `USER-GUIDE.md`. Registered deviation.

6. **REST binding** — UCP's canonical REST binding uses the Catalog POST paths,
   `PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}` for `update_checkout`, and bare `id` path
   parameters for Checkout and Order resources. These depart from GoDaddy
   platform URI, method, and parameter naming conventions. Registered deviation.
info.title: UCP Commerce API (GoDaddy)

UCP-native `dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.search` capability
(`search_catalog` in the canonical REST binding). Returns products
whose products and variants may carry GoDaddy-extension fields
(`input_schema`, `renewal_price`, `tier`/`plan`) when the calling
platform has negotiated the corresponding extension capability — see
"Capability negotiation" above. Buyer auth is optional here: linking a
buyer first returns customer-specific catalog/pricing when available,
but anonymous search is supported.

Negotiated `com.godaddy.shopping.domain` discovery uses the explicit
`domains[]` request defined by its reusable schema, not `query`, and
invokes this operation. Results may include relevant alternative domain
Products in addition to requested-domain matches; every Product identifies
whether it is a requested match or a suggestion and carries its own current
availability and price. Unavailable/error requested candidates are
correlated through `messages[]`.
A non-purchasable concept uses the separately negotiated
`com.godaddy.shopping.catalog_action` contract to identify this operation
and its complete request schema. Target purchase responses use returned purchasable product/variant IDs; the
Domain result IDs and prices in examples are
illustrative protocol values only; production values come from Catalog
Query.

post.description:
UCP-native `dev.ucp.shopping.checkout` capability. Version 1 creates
Checkout directly with required `line_items[]` containing selected
Variant IDs; no Cart conversion is advertised. `buyer`/`context` are
optional (a buyer may be linked now, or left anonymous and linked
later, any time before `complete_checkout`). For an authenticated buyer,
the response returns all eligible saved payment instruments in canonical
deterministic handler order. If `payment` is omitted, the first eligible
instrument is selected. If `payment` explicitly selects an instrument,
it must be owned by the buyer and eligible; invalid explicit selection
produces a recoverable error and never silently falls back. The response
`status` reflects the checkout state machine (`incomplete`,
`requires_escalation`, `ready_for_complete`,
`complete_in_progress`, `completed`, `canceled`); `messages[]`
with `requires_buyer_input`/`requires_buyer_review` severity drive
`requires_escalation`, in which case `continue_url` MUST be
present. A line item's extension `input` MUST validate against the
selected variant's `input_schema`. A missing required value or
invalid input is rejected with a `recoverable` message and the
session stays `incomplete` — see `update_checkout` below for the
same rule on subsequent adds.

put.description:
Canonical REST binding names this `update_checkout` and binds it
to **PUT** (idempotent replace of the writable fields), not PATCH.
`line_items[]` is required on update, same as create; fields
marked `ucp_request: omit`/server-only (e.g. `status`, `totals`,
`id`) MUST NOT be sent and are ignored/rejected if present. This
also adds or removes selected Variants in an existing Checkout by
resending the complete `line_items[]` collection.

**Enforcement:** the Checkout application validates each line-item
`input`, when supplied, against the selected variant's `input_schema`.
A missing required value or invalid value keeps the session `incomplete`
with a `recoverable` message. A buyer may also be linked (or changed) on
this call, any time before `complete_checkout` — see "Direct Checkout and
identity linking" above.

**Idempotent replace, not merge:** because `PUT` replaces the
writable fields wholesale, each `line_items[]` entry — including
its `input` (GoDaddy extension field) — MUST be resent in full on every
call, even one only adding or changing `payment`. A replacement payment
selection must identify one eligible saved instrument with
`selected: true`; the response returns all eligible instruments with
exactly that one selected. Omitting a previously-set writable value
clears it; PUT does not merge.

**Unpriceable line items are silently dropped, not a hard
failure:** if a submitted line item's product cannot be priced
(e.g. a stale/unpriceable catalog entry), the business removes it
from the response line_items[] and attaches a `message_warning`
(`code: line_item_removed`) naming its original position rather
than rejecting the whole update; see `checkout_line_item_removed_pricing_failure`.

post.description:
Transitions `ready_for_complete` -> `complete_in_progress` ->
`completed`. `payment` is `required` at complete time (per
`checkout.json`'s `ucp_request.complete: required`); a linked
buyer is also required by this point, whether it was linked at
`create_checkout` or on any `update_checkout` call up to now —
see "Direct Checkout and identity linking" above. On success
the returned checkout includes `order` (`order_confirmation`:
`id` + `permalink_url`); the platform then calls
`GET /orders/{id}` for full order detail.

**This call can also escalate.** If the payment handler returns a
pending/challenge result (for example, 3D Secure), the response is
`requires_escalation` with a payment-handler-defined `continue_url`
(see `checkout_requires_escalation_at_complete`). This is distinct
from the out-of-band account page used to add a missing saved payment
method. Poll `get_checkout` after the payment-authentication interaction;
it resolves to `complete_in_progress` → `completed`, back to
`ready_for_complete` on failure, or remains `requires_escalation`
while pending.
